sammendrag: Using population-wide registry data from Norway, this article examines the labour market implications of the gender gap in school performance by analysing how returns to lower secondary GPA vary by gender and social origin. Overall, high academic performance is associated with high income and lower unemployment probabilities for both men and women. However, the results indicate that men enjoy a compensatory advantage, suggesting that school grades are less crucial for their labour market success. In contrast, high academic performance appears to offset some of the economic disadvantages women face in the labour market. Importantly, however, this is only the case for women from high social origins. In terms of unemployment, both men and women from high-income families benefit from a compensatory advantage, suggesting that poor grades are less detrimental to the labour market opportunities of individuals from high-income backgrounds.
tittel: The value of good grades. Gender and social origin differences in returns to lower secondary school performance
